title: Er det tid for guttetur?
subtitle: Is it time for a boys’ trip?
lead: Seven versions of “no,” chosen at random. In October 2021, I changed the answer to “yes,” then fixed the array index.
paragraphs: The March 2021 version picked a response at random from a list of seven. They included “Nope,” “Helst ikke” and “Kanskje vente til pandemien er over?”

On 27 October, I replaced the list with “Ja!” but left the random index calculation unchanged. It still selected a position from zero to six, so most positions no longer contained an answer. The next commit set the index to zero.
The version here lets you switch between March and October. It cycles through the earlier responses instead of choosing randomly.

title: Retrospective.fun
subtitle: Every retro remembers the last one.
lead: An online tool for team retrospectives, with notes and actions that carry from one session to the next.
paragraphs: I started Retrospective.fun in 2017 and still work on it. It keeps the notes and actions from a retrospective available when the team meets again.
Teams can choose a meeting format, group what people wrote, record actions and refer back to earlier discussions. Formats such as Sailboat and Six Thinking Hats each have their own sequence.

title: NoteGame → NoteQuest
subtitle: My daughter’s game, from an idea I tried in 2023.
lead: My daughter develops NoteQuest with AI assistance. I look after the backend and hosting.
paragraphs: In 2023, I tried building a game for learning to read notes. NoteGame showed a note on a staff and asked you to pick the right answer. I left it unfinished.
A few years later, my daughter took up the idea and built NoteQuest using AI-assisted development. She develops the game; I provide the backend, hosting and engineering support.
